name: Covered calls on the S&P 500 (buy-write, BXM)

origin.source_title: Return and Risk of CBOE Buy Write Monthly Index (Journal of Derivatives 10(2), 35-42)

how_it_works.simple: Own the S&P 500 and every month sell someone the right to buy it from you at today's price. You keep the fee, but you give up any gain above that price.
how_it_works.analogy: Like renting out a spare room: steady rent, but if a buyer offers a fortune for the house that month, you have already promised it at a fixed price.
how_it_works.precise: Cboe's BXM index holds the S&P 500 and writes the near-term at-the-money call, generally on the third Friday of each month, holding it to expiry and cash-settling. Index options are usually priced above the volatility that follows (the volatility risk premium), so the written calls earn more on average than they pay out.

rule: On each monthly option expiry, hold the S&P 500 and sell one at-the-money one-month S&P 500 call per unit held; keep the premium; repeat at the next expiry.
data_needed: Cboe BXM index daily history (free CSV)
economic_rationale: Investors pay up for index options as insurance, so option sellers earn a premium for bearing crash risk (the volatility risk premium).
why_it_might_fail: The upside is capped, so it lags in strong bull markets and still takes most of a crash. The index ignores costs and taxes. Retail funds and bots often present the premium as 'yield', which it is not: it is payment for giving up gains.

reported_results.source: Callan Associates (2006), An Historical Evaluation of the CBOE S&P 500 BuyWrite Index Strategy
reported_results.notes: Annualised compound return 11.77% for BXM vs 11.67% for the S&P 500; annualised standard deviation 9.29% vs 13.89%; annualised Sharpe ratio 0.77 vs 0.51; skew -1.24 vs -0.44. Index values, no trading costs. Study commissioned via Cboe.

post_publication_evidence: Not checked by us yet. The 1988 to 2006 window ends before the 2009 to 2021 bull market, when a capped strategy would be expected to lag; Cboe's free BXM history lets us check this.

relevance.reason: Covered call income funds and bots are among the most marketed retail strategies, so Verify needs a fair benchmark for what this premium has actually paid.

research.notes: Cboe publishes BXM daily history free at https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/BXM_History.csv; we have not added a fetcher. Added by Amanda's library batch on 2026-10-25 (options, intraday and equity anomalies that retail traders and bots claim to use).
